svg.text: PART C - branch comparator: 33-bit subtract with signed/unsigned extension (sketch: 'right/unsigned subtract, 33 bit')
PART D - next-PC logic (fetch_pc_o = redirect ? target : PC + 4)
PART E / F - branch stall logic and the EX -> WB pipeline register
Fig P5 - EX stage: branch comparator, next-PC logic, branch-stall logic and EX/WB register
From your 'High-level EX stage block diagram': C = branch comparator, D = next-PC logic, E = branch stall logic, F = EX/WB register. (A, B = Fig P3.)
The unsigned bit flips the sign extension so a single 33-bit subtract gives the right 'less than' for both signed and unsigned compares.
branch_taken = (branch_cond & is_branch) | jal | jalr -> also drives wb_branch_o (Part E) and the flush shift register (Fig P1)
squash_ex (this instruction was fetched behind a taken branch)
squash_ex = 1 -> the instruction currently in EX is a wrong-path instruction: its register-write, memory-write and branch_taken are forced to 0.
captures ex_result etc. on clk; holds on stall_read; cleared on reset
Outputs go to Fig P6 (WB / load-store unit).
